gaps.note: A commercial break edit hides the continuation of the founder's answer to Anne's concern.

stage_a.note: Enthusiastic and positive delivery while explaining the benefits of the stem cell banking service.
Very high engaged excitement when discussing the science and potential to extend pet lives.
Friendly, approachable, smiles frequently, and brings puppies to interact with the panel.

venture.description: A stem cell banking and regenerative medicine service for pets, collecting cells during routine spay and neuter procedures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder introduces himself, his company Gallant, and directs the panel's attention to a basket of puppies.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder hands out a puppy to each investor, engaging in lighthearted social interaction with the panel.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder continues his pitch, asking the panel to imagine the puppies suffering from age-related ailments in the future.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with surprise as an actor dressed as the Grim Reaper enters the set.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder assists as the Grim Reaper actor takes the puppies back from the investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the stem cell banking process, the benefits of regenerative medicine, and makes his investment ask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes that the situation with the high valuation is not going to end well.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori assumes the company must have fantastic sales given the high valuation and asks about them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains they have two divisions, therapeutics and consumer banking, noting the consumer side launches soon.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin echoes Mark's earlier sentiment, joking that he knows how the pitch will end.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks the founder to share his history and background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder details his previous successful venture, an online dog sitting platform that generated significant sales and merged.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for the specific name of the founder's previous company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder names his previous company as DogVacay, which is now called Rover.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what the founder's background training is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains his neuroscience background and how he hired top minds in veterinary regenerative medicine to secure patents.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori confirms he has patents and asks what they cover technically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the science of stem cells depleting with age and how his patent isolates them from reproductive tissue.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes that he wants to use the procedure on himself instead of dogs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder jokes back, recommending Mark undergo the procedure, leading to shared laughter about neutering.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges the premise, arguing that if stem cell injections worked so simply, injuries would never matter in sports.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder briefly acknowledges Mark's point without directly refuting the challenge to the science.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark presses further, asking why the treatment isn't already standard practice if it actually worked.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne steps in to defend the founder's premise, noting that while not standard for humans, it is researched in animals.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin pivots to the consumer business model and asks how much it costs the customer to get the kit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states the cost to the consumer is an annual storage fee of $95.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies if the initial kit is free as long as the annual storage fee is paid.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the pricing structure and explains that veterinarians also make revenue by performing the procedure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne points out that the company instantly loses money on the initial customer acquisition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder concedes that they lose money initially.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the exact cost to perform the stem cell extraction.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states that the total cost for the kit and shipping is about $275.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne asks if that $275 figure includes the payment to the veterinarian.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder clarifies it does not include the vet payment, but notes most vets do it for free.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the company's current monthly burn rate is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they are burning $400,000 a month, primarily on research and development.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne asks if the company has any other investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms they have raised a total of $10 million from top investors.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks what the valuation was on their last funding round.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states the last valuation was $25 million, which matches his current ask.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how much more capital the company will need to raise when they officially launch.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder estimates they will need to raise another $25 million in 2021.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne expresses deep concern that losing money on every initial sale will cause the company to sink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder begins to address Anne's concern but his response is hidden by a commercial break edit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: After the break, Anne repeats her anxiety about the unit economics and the risk of the company sinking.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder deflects the unit economics concern by pointing out they are well-capitalized with good investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne forcefully challenges him, stating that capital doesn't matter if he can't sell anything profitably.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne explains that at 23andMe they make money on every kit, and losing money initially means years to recapture value.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder concedes that it does take a little while to recapture the initial loss.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond declares he is out, citing Anne's nervousness as his primary reason.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder attempts to appeal to Daymond's love for pets.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges his pet connections but reiterates his exit decision based on Anne's concerns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder politely thanks Daymond.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne asks the founder to give her hope on how the $275 cost will decrease over time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder suggests raising the price to $399, which would lower volume but stop them from hemorrhaging money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne agrees that raising prices is a good idea to prevent the company from losing money on sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder elaborates on his strategy to lower barriers to entry initially to create virality in a new market.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne shares 23andMe's history of launching at a high price to let early adopters work out the kinks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder acknowledges that at scale there might be a better pricing structure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin presents two different offers, one with equity and options, and another with equity and a perpetual royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder comments on Kevin's creative structuring, appreciating the incentive while waiting for others to speak.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin boasts that his offer is, of course, very clever.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating he believes in stem cells but feels the storage and consumer side is not figured out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Mark for his time.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Anne proposes a joint offer with Lori for $500k at 8% equity, emphasizing their combined ability to reach consumers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reacts positively to the joint offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori formally joins Anne's offer, stating her belief in the business and Anne as a partner.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder expresses his desire to make the deal work but notes he must protect his employees' equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin pressures the founder to make a decision between the standing offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder counters Anne and Lori, asking if they would lower their equity requirement to 4%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark laughs at the founder's counter-offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori consults with Anne, asking if they should counter the founder's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori revises their joint offer, asking the founder if he would accept 5% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder immediately accepts the revised joint offer from Anne and Lori.

exchanges.label: standard of care in humans vs animals
initial acquisition loss and burn rate
losing money on kits and pricing strategy

decisions.note: Exits because Anne is nervous about the consumer acquisition costs.

decisions.terms: $500k for 2% equity plus 2% in options, OR $500k for 1% equity plus a $10 royalty per kit in perpetuity.
decisions.note: Loves the space and brings value; offers two creative structures.
Believes in stem cells but thinks the storage and consumer side is not figured out.
Believes in long-term potential and consumer reach with Lori.
Joins Anne's offer, believing in the business and the partnership.
Counters Anne and Lori to protect his employees and early scientists.
Revises the joint offer with Anne to 5% equity after the founder's counter.
Accepts the revised joint offer from Anne and Lori.

record.notes: The founder's pitch is briefly interrupted by an actor dressed as the Grim Reaper, which the founder incorporates into his presentation. A commercial break edit hides the beginning of the founder's response to Anne's concern about unit economics.
